properties.decision:
RULED by Anthony 2026-09-06 ("go with your above recommendations for v0.50.0"), item 3 of the v0.50.0 plan: proposal ① adopted — every constructor accepts optional `status` and `approver`; a status past the landing default (a Decision `accepted`, a Requirement off `proposed`, a DesignRule with `enforced` stated) is REFUSED unless `approver` names a Contributor, so the signature is present rather than assumed and dec:certainty-derived holds in one call; proposal ② adopted — add_verification takes `verifies` (targets), `status`, `findings`, `last_run_at`; add_epoch's planned form is plan_epoch (shipped in v0.49.0); proposal ③ (a "wire this capability" call) NOT taken in this increment. The status SETTERS (set_decision_status, set_requirement_status) gain optional `approver` and, when a settling status is written without one, REPORT that the write carries nobody's name rather than refuse — the existing surface has consumers, and acknowledge_gap_by is the precedent for report-not-refuse on an optional approver. Fresh evidence the same day: fact:an-accepted-status-written-without-its-approver-failed-the-intent-gate-in-ci.

WHAT WAS ON THE TABLE (recorded 2026-09-04 as brainstorming). Ideas 2, 3 and 4 from the qs project agent, 2026-09-04, corroborated by dev_storyflow's constructor table of the same day.

THE COMPLAINT, qs: "MANY SMALL CALLS PER FACT. Recording one verification took FOUR TO SIX calls (`add_verification`, `set_verification_status`, `verifies` per target, `link_artifact` per file). Recording one decision THE USER HAD ALREADY MADE took `add_decision` then `set_decision_status`, and DOING BOTH IN ONE PARALLEL BATCH IS REFUSED BECAUSE THEY ARE UNORDERED. `add_capability` accepts `status`; `add_decision` and `add_requirement` do not accept an initial status EVEN WHEN THE OWNER'S WORD IS IN HAND."

⭐ THE BATCHING NOTE IS THE PART THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN ERGONOMICS. The two calls cannot be issued together, because a harness emits a batch unordered and `set_decision_status` may run before the node exists — which is `fact:the-parallel-batch-class-recurred-because-only-its-instance-was-fixed`. So the cost is not one extra call, it is a FORCED SERIAL ROUND TRIP on the single commonest capture in the tool.

THEIR THREE PROPOSALS:
① `add_decision(..., status="accepted", decided_by=<contributor>)` — and the same for requirements — REFUSED UNLESS A CONTRIBUTOR IS NAMED, "so the certainty rule still holds but one call does the work".
② `add_verification(verifies=[...], status, findings, last_run_at)` — "the common case is 'I just ran it and here is what it found'".
③ A "wire this capability" call: allocate + realizes + verifies in one step, which would also collapse the three-findings-for-one-missing-edge shape they reported separately.

🛑 THE RULE THIS HAS TO SURVIVE, and ① is deliberately shaped to survive it. `dec:certainty-derived` says certainty is DERIVED FROM STATUS, so an agent promoting a status on the user's behalf FORGES THEIR SIGNATURE — which is why `add_decision` lands `proposed` and why the brainstorm skill tells you to verify it did. ⭐ Their proposal does not weaken that: it makes the contributor MANDATORY when a status is passed, so the signature is present rather than assumed. Whether a named contributor is sufficient evidence of the user's word, or whether only a separate deliberate act counts, is exactly the open question — RULED: the named approver is the signature; it is the same AUTHORED_BY role=approver edge the intent gate reads.

⚠️ AND `add_capability` ALREADY DOES THIS, which is either the precedent or the inconsistency depending on how it is read. dev_storyflow measured four sibling constructors giving four different answers to "what status does this land in", and `add_capability` honouring an explicit status is one of them. So the surface has already decided this once, for one type, without the rule being argued.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the four-to-six calls per verification is dominated by the status or by the EDGES (`verifies` per target, `link_artifact` per file). Only ② and ③ address the edges, and nobody has counted which half of their traffic was which — so the cheapest fix may be the bulk edge forms rather than the status field.
properties.name: DECIDED — constructors accept the owner's word in one call: optional `status` + `approver` on every constructor, a status past the landing default REFUSED without an approver; add_verification takes verifies/status/findings/last_run_at; the status setters take `approver` too and REPORT its absence
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill; recorded as an idea, nothing promoted. Kept separate from the companion-CLI idea because this one turns on a governance rule (dec:certainty-derived) rather than on the no-file-IO boundary, and separate from the constructor-naming fact because that records a measured defect while this asks a design question the user must rule on.
